release_review.summary: Compatibility epoch 16 requires the shared model catalog query and compact model-selection preferences, including Gemini and model-specific image capabilities. Older Desktop and Runtime combinations must not interpret an empty expanded model list as an unconfigured brand provider. The matched v0.12.0 release pair retains epoch 15 Web Service management, epoch 14 CodeSpace origins, and epoch 13 native HTTP/stream behavior.
checked_surfaces: Flower settings in Desktop and Env App use the same administrator-only read-only model_catalog endpoint and offline generated catalog. Brand selection persists exclusions and sparse overrides; Runtime startup atomically converts old profiles without changing current or thread models. OpenRouter keeps explicit selection, Ollama resolves installed tool models without a persistent inventory, and per-model image input includes prepared DeepSeek Vision through published Floret v7.9.2. Gemini credentials, effort/budget controls, image input, and tool thought signatures use the existing provider boundary. Desktop attach/start, Local UI health, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, and SSH runtime bootstrap negotiate epoch 16 before allowing profile exchange.

Floret v7.9.2 public inspection, WAL snapshots, deferred Host activation, and restore preparation own canonical storage and execution. Product and read-state stores share the readiness generation; backing_up and restoring remain Flower-only maintenance states in Env App, Desktop, Runtime Service, and sys.ping. Administrator-confirmed restoration uses a durable complete-set replacement journal, preserves prior data and queued inputs, and invalidates old execution and approval. New user submissions fetch the storage generation; persisted outbox retries retain their original generation and remain copyable after rejection. The flower-title-generation-v1 title contract and all transport review surfaces remain required.

Flower HTTP lists, details, and live summaries carry Floret title_generation. Desktop and Env App require the same canonical title contract; the existing compatibility handshake rejects older epoch combinations. Title text, status, and generation share one ThreadCache summary owner independently of runtime views.

DeepSeek uses the published Floret stateless Responses gateway, fixed Agent hosted search, and existing supplemental-context privacy fences without changing the Desktop or Runtime protocol. Redeven consumes published github.com/floegence/floret/v7 v7.9.2 with GOWORK=off and exact module checksums; every production Agent binds one immutable RunLabels snapshot at construction so fresh execution and continuations share Floret's provider-host injection point, while provider admission and policy refresh never rebind the admitted permission snapshot; committed final provider usage carries canonical whole-thread cache token totals through the live event boundary without a downstream ledger, while projected requests preserve the last confirmed totals; Floret-native web_fetch owns secure public-text fetching, parsing, output policy, and typed Activity with a bounded preview while ignoring page icons, and Redeven owns current product authorization plus one Searching indicator that animates only while the fetch is running; runtime startup atomically converges legacy UTF-8 tool-result Raw data, exact RunID identity, and every dispatching, retrying, or unknown effect into one typed terminal failure before the Host is available and removes terminal forked Effect Attempt history only when source-thread ancestry and execution identity are verified; canonical Effect results converge from one committed entry with valid UTF-8 text, segmented records preserve active-turn recovery without whole-state rewrites, published SQLite maintenance reclaims eligible free pages before the single runtime open, root inventory supplies summary-only list projection, cumulative typed Activity preserves terminal call descriptions through results and restart, additive terminal operation and safe byte/cursor facts keep every terminal call inspectable without exposing interactive input, user cancellation binds the selected Turn’s current Run atomically with settlement, typed SubAgent operation Activity preserves the exact action, ordered targets, counts, and wait timeout through restart; child current views replace only the parent Subagent inventory and never enter the root thread list; admitted child mutations do not perform post-effect List, View, or title calls, user Stop atomically records a terminal aborted turn and seals late provider, tool, and save-point work, canonical terminal items replace stream-only text without appending run-level output, stale canonical snapshots cannot replace a newer terminal view, canonical queue and interaction acceptance precedes visible success, unknown effects fail once and cannot be replayed, delete and shutdown fence active subtrees and effect dispatch, migration v2 through v10 remains atomic and fail-closed, verified fork context is rewritten to destination Thread identity without a downstream repair path, ordered views stay monotonic across live updates and restart, new tool history preserves complete Engine-authored call reasoning and hosted assistant fragment boundaries so source and fork continuation survive restart without duplicate calls; existing corrupt history is not rewritten, and no replace, go.work, sibling source path, copied contract, internal import, or Floret schema access exists

Floret ThreadView.RunID, ThreadItem.RunID, ThreadInteraction.RunID, and RunProgress are the exact execution identity and phase source; Redeven does not infer historical run identity from the current run, TurnID, message content, or a parallel model-I/O stream

Floret v7.9.2 owns append-only canonical context plus full Turn-surface render lineages: forked context takes destination Thread identity from the canonical entry while preserving historical Turn and Run identity; Redeven freezes the persisted model, reasoning, System Prompt, tools, adapter, and context policy at new-Turn admission, treats request model fields only as consistency checks, keeps the original user objective in canonical history, appends mutable environment facts as durable per-turn UserInput.Context snapshots without rewriting an earlier request prefix, and starts each new context policy without the previous model's latest usage while preserving cumulative whole-thread totals
A natural provider stop completes a Flower Turn; ordinary tools continue, ask_user waits and resumes the same immutable surface, and settings or product-version changes affect only a later Turn

Provider history preserves ask_user as one Assistant tool call plus matching Tool result; public answers occur once in that result, secret values remain ephemeral, and provider-context v8 keeps typed historical tool facts stable across later Turns without restoring removed definitions or hashing runtime and journal entry identities

Floret v7.9.2 strictly validates model arguments and allows at most two regeneration attempts with complete canonical call/result pairs. Invalid ask_user arguments do not create an interaction or Activity; UI filtering never removes provider history. Exhaustion retains control_error and generated text with a localized retry action, while projector, storage, and unknown-effect failures remain terminal. Historical control failures cannot create pending input, and Flower rejects missing, null, or empty typed questions before ThreadCache.

Historical tool Activity is projected from persisted canonical presentation without consulting the current registry; removed tools use one neutral safe presentation and are not restored as compatibility definitions

Every Floret Run transition publishes the new exact RunID in preparing before provider dispatch and resets attempt ownership; Redeven forwards preparing, waiting_response, streaming, reasoning, and assistant growth directly without polling, inferred progress, or terminal backfill

Floret v7.9.2 publishes an unresolved approval or user-input interaction together with the matching active projection in one transition: waiting interactions clear run_progress while other active summaries retain it; local waiters are reserved before durable admission so response handling resumes the existing execution without duplicate provider dispatch

Floret v7.9.2 publishes validated command presentation and tool settlement directly from its existing thread actor before output or turn completion. Desktop and Env App consume unchanged ThreadView fields; failed tools default collapsed and retain manual disclosure choices. Public API, Runtime Service protocol, compatibility epoch, and storage schema are unchanged.
Floret ThreadService is the only lifecycle boundary for View, Send, Respond, Cancel, Retry, PromoteQueued, and Subscribe
Each Floret thread has one in-memory ThreadRuntime owner; its canonical journal is the only durable lifecycle fact source
Redeven persists only product settings, authorization audit, uploads, read state, and the contiguous v1-to-v2 migration import boundary
Redeven handlers authorize and map typed requests without admission receipts, authority barriers, recovery handles, or projection mirrors
Flower uses one workspace SSE, summary/detail-separated ThreadCache, ComposerDraftStore, short-lived IndexedDB TransportOutbox, and LiveTransport
Thread selection never owns execution or reconnects transport; summary updates never overwrite typed detail
Unknown irreversible tool effects terminate their Turn with effect_outcome_unknown and have no replay or retry surface

Redeven consumes only published Flowersec Go and Core v5.1.0 plus Floe Webapp v0.50.6 for both the Desktop shell and Env App, with exact module checksums and no replace, file, link, workspace, portal, sibling checkout, private import, or copied transport implementation

Public Local UI uses independent HTTPS and Flowersec WSS listeners with exact Host and Origin admission, one-shot artifacts, isolated concurrent windows, explicit terminal failure, and cleanup of pending authorization, handlers, sessions, and notification sinks; the private Desktop document bridge instead uses the isolated flowersec-private-loopback/1 browser and Go APIs behind exact numeric-loopback and per-process bridge-token admission

Each remote or local accepted session registers the final Flowersec SessionHandlers, RPC, ByteStream, and terminal/live_v1 boundaries directly; outbound terminal notification sinks attach to the established Flowersec RPC peer and detach idempotently when that session ends

Desktop attach and start, CA-free private bridge health, optional public device CA trust, startup reports, sys.ping, Env App maintenance, SSH runtime bootstrap, independent public WSS, terminal history recovery, and consecutive Desktop bridge sessions remain covered by focused transport contracts

Flowersec ConnectionController remains the only reconnect owner; secure-session retry uses Floe Webapp replaceConnection so an old asynchronous close cannot overwrite a new controller generation, while Redeven supplies artifact acquisition, authorization, permissions, product RPC handlers, and post-session business recovery without a second reconnect state machine or alternate carrier path

The desktop-placement-http2-v1 boundary remains unchanged. Runtime Service protocol_version is redeven-runtime-v2 at compatibility_epoch 16; Desktop verifies Runtime Service, the redeven-desktop-placement-h2/1 private bridge, Catalog, Local UI, package identity, and a unique managed process before a direct lifecycle operation succeeds
Gateway is an optional access component and never prepares, starts, stops, updates, reinstalls, or supervises a managed Runtime

Published ReDevPlugin 3.0.31 prepares validated installed Worker modules during process startup before an Env App session exists, while authenticated recovery remains the execution authority. The released bounded document cache retains only hash-matched bytes and revalidates trust. Workbench hidden and offscreen first commits, exact-slot retry cleanup, real Desktop runtime restart, and preparation latency are covered without changing Runtime Service protocol, Rust IPC, or plugin author API.

Desktop CodeSpace windows and system-browser openings share the selected EnvironmentSession route and generation-bound Runtime handler. ID-only browser intent mints a single-use entry on an isolated cs-<profile>.localhost origin; Host-only browser cookies never reach Runtime or the editor. Epoch 14 rejects older runtimes that only accept numeric-loopback presentation origins. Entry expiry, HTTP resources, WebSockets, AccessGate, environment disposal, file save and terminal execution are covered without replaying application traffic.

Web Service observation, action capabilities and reviewed plans distinguish missing resources, unavailable inspection and ownership conflicts. Uninstall journals preserve per-resource results; detach atomically archives management and revokes active proxy streams without stopping business processes. Registry portforward_registry_v2 advances from schema 3 to 4 without moving existing resources or changing TemplateSpec v6. All Activity and Workbench entries use the same review drawer and instance resource boundary.

Floret v7.9.2 renders canonical references and accepted context snapshots into the actual provider history, including continuation, retry, fork, restart, and compaction. ResourceRef remains opaque and secret answers remain ephemeral. The contiguous v9-to-v10 migration validates existing records without rewriting historical journal bytes; provider-context v8 establishes an explicit projection boundary. Environment cards distinguish the user-selected device from the tool execution environment and include the existing routing skill at admission. Terminal Activity shows actual result target and execution location without inferring remote execution from a local CLI command. Existing Desktop/Runtime wire shapes and compatibility epoch remain unchanged.
